symptom: A test written with a bare `@throws` fails on the very exception it was written to expect, reporting "exception during execution" and "no assertions"
cause: `mxcli test` treats a test as a throws-test only when the annotation carries a NON-EMPTY message (`generator_endpoint.go`, `if tc.Throws != ""`), so a bare `@throws` is silently ignored and the exception propagates as a failure. The message itself is **never compared** — `@throws 'ZZZ-NOT-THE-REAL-MESSAGE'` passes against any error — so it documents intent rather than asserting it
insight: Write `@throws '<description>'` and give the test its meaning with a CONTROL — the same call with input that must NOT throw — because the annotation alone only proves something was raised, not what. Two separate defects to fix: a bare `@throws` should be a parse error rather than silently dropped, and the message should either be matched or documented as unmatched (the annotations reference shows `@throws 'validation failed'`, which reads as a match). Found while asserting #261's `or error` at run time
